## Ctx.renderPaidMedia() method

Sends Stars-locked photo/video content using the page `<g-paid-media>` block.

**Signature:**

```typescript
renderPaidMedia(keyboard?: ITInlineKb | null, data?: ITData | null, AGBaseId?: string | null, options?: Parameters<Ctx[`replyWithPaidMedia`]>[2] | null): Promise<grammy_types.Message.PaidMediaMessage>;
```

## Remarks

Fail-fast validation (`Ctx.assertPaidMedia`<!-- -->) runs BEFORE any API call on the COMPILED block — programmer errors always throw, never fall back. Each item `src` is resolved through the instance media jail (`this.resolveMedia`<!-- -->: local files become `InputFile` uploads, URLs and `file_id` values pass through) and sent with its caption as HTML.

Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderInvoice`<!-- -->): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`<!-- -->, reported to `notifySendError`<!-- -->, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`<!-- -->, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`<!-- -->). There is no degraded fallback content for paywalls, so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched — the `catch` below observes only and never swallows, because swallowing would hide a paywall send failure from the caller.

## Example 1


```typescript
async handleCallbackQueryData() {
  const kb = this.inlineKeyboard((k) => k.text("OK", "ok"))
  await this.renderPaidMedia(kb, {teaser: `t.jpg`, full: `v.mp4`})
}
```

## Example 2


```typescript
async handleBuyContent() {
  // Template: <g-paid-media stars="100"><g-media type="photo" src="{{teaser}}">Bayar untuk membuka</g-media></g-paid-media>
  await this.renderPaidMedia(null, {teaser: `teaser.jpg`})
}
```
